claims.text: Clean Architecture draws a system as rings: business rules at the centre, then use cases, then adapters, then frameworks and the database at the edge. Central rule: nothing in the inner rings names an adapter or an edge framework (ASP.NET Core, EF Core); adapters are written with them.
claims.source_hint: refs/dotnet-docs architecture/modern-web-apps-azure/common-web-application-architectures.md (concentric circles, dependencies toward the centre); glossary clean-architecture

claims.text: A use case is one thing the application does for its user, with the rules for doing it; PlaceOrderAsync and CancelOrderAsync in OrderService are Đơn Hàng's use cases.
The ports IOrderRepository and INotifier belong to the core: they are declared in DonHang.Domain, because the use cases (OrderService) are the code that needs them; nothing outside declares them.

At stage-1 OrderService.PlaceOrderAsync throws ArgumentException when items is empty, builds an Order with Status "new", calls repository.AddAsync, repository.SaveChangesAsync, then notifier.Send(order.Id, "order placed").
At stage-1 OrderService names Order, OrderItem, IOrderRepository and INotifier but no controller, repository class, EF Core, ASP.NET Core or logging type.
DonHang.Domain.csproj at stage-1 contains no ProjectReference and no PackageReference; Order, OrderItem and OrderService all live in DonHang.Domain.

Without a ProjectReference or PackageReference, code in a .NET project cannot name types from another project or NuGet package (the build fails); it still sees the .NET base library through the implicit framework reference.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs: MSBuild project references / PackageReference; C# compiler error CS0246 for an unknown type

claims.text: DonHang.Api.csproj references DonHang.Domain and DonHang.Infrastructure and the package Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.JwtBearer; DonHang.Infrastructure.csproj references DonHang.Domain; OrdersController is in DonHang.Api, EfOrderRepository and LoggingNotifier in DonHang.Infrastructure.

Layered, hexagonal and Clean all keep HTTP, business rules and data access apart; classic layering lets the business layer depend on the data-access layer, while hexagonal and Clean make data access depend on the rules through a port the rules declare.

Clean and hexagonal keep the same direction: nothing in the core names an adapter. Hexagonal's words are about the edge (ports, adapters); Clean adds names for the rings inside the core (business rules, use cases). One system can fit both.
The rings describe dependency direction, not a count of projects; a project boundary is one way to make the compiler check the rule, not a requirement of Clean Architecture.
